questiontext.text: What is the sociological definition of "Friendship"?

generalfeedback.text: Friendship is a voluntary personal bond based on affection, mutual respect, and trust.

answer.text: A compulsory legal contract signed in a magistrate court

feedback.text: Incorrect. Friendship is a voluntary personal bond based on affection, mutual respect, and trust.

answer.text: A voluntary, mutual relationship of affection, trust, respect, and companionship between individuals

feedback.text: Correct! Friendship is a voluntary personal bond based on affection, mutual respect, and trust.

answer.text: An association of people who belong to the same military regiment

feedback.text: Incorrect. Friendship is a voluntary personal bond based on affection, mutual respect, and trust.

answer.text: A commercial partnership for buying petroleum shares

feedback.text: Incorrect. Friendship is a voluntary personal bond based on affection, mutual respect, and trust.

questiontext.text: What is "Peer Pressure"?

generalfeedback.text: Peer pressure is the social influence exerted by contemporaries to adopt group behaviors and attitudes.

answer.text: The physical atmospheric pressure measured by a barometer

feedback.text: Incorrect. Peer pressure is the social influence exerted by contemporaries to adopt group behaviors and attitudes.

answer.text: The psychological and social influence exerted by age-mates to conform to their group attitudes and behaviors

feedback.text: Correct! Peer pressure is the social influence exerted by contemporaries to adopt group behaviors and attitudes.

answer.text: The hydraulic force of water in a dam

feedback.text: Incorrect. Peer pressure is the social influence exerted by contemporaries to adopt group behaviors and attitudes.

answer.text: The chemical reaction between acids and bases

feedback.text: Incorrect. Peer pressure is the social influence exerted by contemporaries to adopt group behaviors and attitudes.

questiontext.text: Which of the following is a classic demonstration of POSITIVE peer pressure?

generalfeedback.text: Inspiring friends to read, study, and develop positive intellectual habits is positive peer pressure.

answer.text: Urging a friend to skip morning school devotion to play video games

feedback.text: Incorrect. Inspiring friends to read, study, and develop positive intellectual habits is positive peer pressure.

answer.text: A group of classmates challenging one another to read one novel every week and excel in English Studies

feedback.text: Correct! Inspiring friends to read, study, and develop positive intellectual habits is positive peer pressure.

answer.text: Pressuring a student to steal money from their mother's handbag

feedback.text: Incorrect. Inspiring friends to read, study, and develop positive intellectual habits is positive peer pressure.

answer.text: Laughing at a classmate who wears neat school sandals

feedback.text: Incorrect. Inspiring friends to read, study, and develop positive intellectual habits is positive peer pressure.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A genuine friend is loyal, truthful, respects boundaries, and supports positive values.

feedback.text: Incorrect. "R" stands for *Remove yourself*—walking away calmly when companions refuse to respect your refusal.
